root_idea.summary: The root centers on cleanness, purity, and the removal of defilement.
root_idea.development: Its meanings extend from physical cleanliness and washing to ritual purification, moral integrity, spiritual purification, and things that purify or are purified.

senses.definition: To become free from menstrual bleeding; to become pure after the discharge stops.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quranic menstrual context, this Form I use denotes the cessation of the discharge, distinguished from the subsequent self-purification expressed by Form V.

senses.definition: To cleanse or purify someone or something from physical dirt, impurity, or defilement; to wash.
senses.usage_conditions: Used with objects such as a house, clothing, or people. In the clothing expression, it is also interpreted as shortening garments to prevent them from trailing and becoming soiled.

senses.definition: To purify the heart, soul, or conduct by removing sin, unbelief, or moral corruption.
senses.usage_conditions: This is a figurative or spiritual extension of cleansing and includes purification understood as right direction and sound conduct.

senses.definition: To cleanse or purify oneself by washing; to perform ritual purification.
senses.usage_conditions: Includes using water or its substitute, ablution, ritual washing, and self-cleansing after menstrual impurity.

senses.definition: To remove oneself from impurity, sin, or blameworthy conduct; to purify oneself spiritually.
senses.usage_conditions: The expression can be used derisively by opponents of those claiming such purity, as in the Quranic accounts of Lot's people.

senses.definition: Purer; more free from impurity, blame, or moral objection.
senses.usage_conditions: A comparative evaluation; in social or legal contexts, purity can yield the contextual sense of being more proper or lawful.

senses.definition: Pure and purifying; especially able to remove impurity.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quran it describes water as both clean in itself and suitable as a means of purification, and describes a pure purifying drink.

senses.definition: Purified or cleansed from physical and natural impurities.
senses.usage_conditions: Used of spouses and other created things purified from bodily defilement and the impurities associated with ordinary worldly life.

senses.definition: Cleansed of impurity, falsehood, or corrupt content.
senses.usage_conditions: Used of writings or scripture to indicate freedom from falsehood and defilement rather than literal washing.

senses.definition: Spiritually purified from corrupt conduct, ignorance, or disobedience.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quranic expression concerning those who touch it, the purification is interpreted as purification of the self and moral conduct.

senses.definition: One who purifies or removes another from defiling association and conduct.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quranic use, it denotes being taken away from those who disbelieve and kept distant from their ways.

senses.definition: One who purifies or cleanses himself.
senses.usage_conditions: The Form V active participle may refer to self-cleansing and ritual purification, including the people praised for purifying themselves.

senses.definition: One who purifies the spirit by abandoning sin and adopting righteous conduct.
senses.usage_conditions: The Quranic praise of such people is explicitly understood as purification of the self and spirit.

senses.definition: The act or result of cleansing and purifying; thorough purification.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quranic construction, it denotes comprehensive purification from defilement, especially in the spiritual and ethical sphere.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To be or become clean, free from dirt or filth, or pure.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The classical verb is used for physical cleanliness and, by extension, for spiritual purity.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To make something distant or remote; to put it far away.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A distinct classical transitive use, synonymous with making something remote.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Cleanness, freedom from dirt or filth, or pureness; also the state of purity from menstrual discharge.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Its plural can denote the days of a woman's state of purity between menstrual periods.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A cleansing or purification, especially purification by water.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The term was also applied by Christians to baptism.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To perform the rite of circumcision upon someone.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative or conventional use understood as purifying the person.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To cleanse someone from sin through a prescribed punishment.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The purification is understood as the expiatory effect of a punishment such as stoning.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A means of purifying a sinner, especially repentance.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of an action or means whose effect is purification rather than of water specifically.

other_classical_meanings.definition: That which purifies a sinner through the execution of a prescribed punishment.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized classical interpretation of purification from sin.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The act of performing ritual washing, ablution, or cleansing after relieving oneself.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Includes ghusl, wudu, and istinja as named ritual or practical forms of purification.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The water remaining after purification or ablution has been performed.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized nominal use distinct from the act of purification itself.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The quality or property of being pure and purifying.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An abstract noun describing the quality denoted by طَهُور.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Clean, free from dirt or filth, or pure; of water, clean and suitable for purification.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A general adjective of physical purity and of water fit for cleansing, without implying the stronger instrumental sense of طَهُور in every context.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Pure or free from menstrual discharge.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This use is also expressed without the feminine marker when referring to a woman in this condition.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Free from vice, fault, or low and ignoble habits.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used in constructions describing a person's honor, character, conduct, or moral reputation.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A vessel used for washing, purification, or ablution.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Includes vessels such as a bucket or waterskin; the approved form is مَطْهَرَةٌ rather than مِطْهَرَةٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A house or chamber in which washing and ablution are performed.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: May include a place for wudu, ghusl, or istinja.

cautions: The Quranic Form I and Form V forms in 2:222 reflect a recognized distinction between the stopping of menstrual discharge and subsequent ritual self-purification; the two readings are therefore kept as separate form groups.

طَهُورٌ has both adjectival and quasi-verbal-noun analyses in the classical evidence, with debate over whether its force is simply 'pure' or also 'purifying'; the Quranic sense states the shared lexical result without resolving that grammatical debate.
The assimilated Quranic spelling مُطَّهِّرِينَ is grouped with the regular Form V citation form مُتَطَهِّر because it is an allomorphic realization of the same active participle.
